subject: Follow-up: Atlas Analytics cost profile & discount options
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Sam Lee <sam.lee@atlas-analytics.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 15 Aug 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Atlas Analytics cost profile & discount options

Thanks again for taking time earlier today, Sam — good conversation. Quick recap and a couple of clarifying questions so we can put together a tailored quote.

Short summary of what I heard:
- Primary workloads: chat-based summarization for user transcripts + semantic search reranking.
- Expected token mix you mentioned: ~70% prompt tokens (user/context) / ~30% completion tokens (model output) — please correct if off.
- Near-term ramp: months 1–3 ~12M tokens/mo, months 4–6 ~25M/mo, months 7–12 target ~60M/mo (spike potential up to ~90M/mo if Q4 marketing flows run).
- Main asks: unit economics target and committed-use paths (12/24 mo), and whether Atlas qualifies for the startup program/credits.

Budget anchor & target
- You said procurement is looking for a predictable runway number rather than on-the-spot list rates. You mentioned a target around ~$300–450 per 1M tokens as an internal reference; please confirm final target if different.

What we need from you to make a clean proposal:
1) Confirm monthly ramp (the numbers above or an updated spreadsheet — procurement contact ok to share?).
2) Confirm whether low-latency reserved capacity (dedicated GPUs) is required or if hosted API (best-effort batching) is fine.
3) Any contractual constraints (PO timing, credit card vs invoice, SOC2 / IP terms) we should know up front.

Next steps from my side
- I’m attaching our Redwood-Starter-Program-FAQ and a short starter discount summary. Rishi and Ben (cc) will draft two paths: (A) Starter + 12mo committed discount and (B) 24mo step-down commitment with a growth rebate.
- We’ll include example math at your mid-ramp (60M/mo) and a conservative case (25M/mo).

Attachments: Redwood-Starter-Program-FAQ.pdf

Thanks — I’ll wait for the usage confirmation or the spreadsheet if procurement prefers to send that. Happy to jump on a short follow-up call if useful.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

--
Redwood Inference | Make inference predictable and economical
From: Sam Lee <sam.lee@atlas-analytics.com>

Cc: Atlas Analytics Procurement <procurement@atlas-analytics.com>
Date: Sun, 16 Aug 2026 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Atlas Analytics cost profile & discount options

Thanks Grace — appreciate the recap. A few clarifications:

- Token mix: looks like I overstated the prompt ratio; our actual mix is closer to 60% prompt / 40% completion once we include system messages and longer generated summaries.
- Updated ramp: proto month (pilot) 10M tokens, month 2–3 15–20M/mo, month 4–6 35–45M/mo, target steady-state by month 10–12 ~75M/mo. We have burst scenarios to ~110M/mo for short campaigns.
- Procurement: please include a quote path for both credit-card self-serve and invoice with PO. Our procurement lead is procurement@atlas-analytics.com (CC’d). They prefer a consolidated monthly invoice and standard data residency (US) and SOC2 attestation.

About pricing: internal target is $350/1M tokens for committed usage (that’s what the board would sign off on for a multi-quarter commit). If that’s unrealistic, please provide the closest normalized unit price we can expect under a 12- and 24-month committed path.

I’ve attached a simple usage estimate (Atlas-Usage-Estimate-2026.xlsx) — it has month-by-month guesses. Please treat it as directional; we’ll confirm once legal/procurement engage.

Can you include any startup credits or promotional incentives for companies pre-Series A? We’re between Seed+ and Series A, so any starter credit would help the pilot economics.

Happy to take a 30m follow-up on Friday (Aug 20) if you want to run the numbers live.

—Sam
Sam Lee
Head of Product, Atlas Analytics
sam.lee@atlas-analytics.com
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 16 Aug 2026 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Follow-up: Atlas Analytics cost profile & discount options

Putting some high-level structure behind a quote we can send — writing the ballpark math so Grace can share with Sam. I’ll draft the formal quote once we align on which path they prefer.

Assumptions (per Sam’s clarifications):
- Token mix: 60% prompt / 40% completion
- Expected steady-state: ~75M tokens/mo
- Burst allowance: up to 110M tokens/mo for short windows

List / reference pricing (internal):
- Hosted API list price: $650 per 1M tokens (normalizing prompts+completions into a single token unit for quoting simplicity).

Discounting paths we can offer (non-final, negotiable):
A) Starter + Short commit (12 months)
- One-time Starter credit: $5,000 applied against first invoice (for Seed/early stage companies meeting criteria)
- 12mo committed usage: tiered discounts: 25% off list up to 50M/mo committed, 32% off list for >50M/mo committed
- Effective unit price examples: at 50M/mo commitment -> $650 * (1 - 0.25) = $487.5/1M; at 75M/mo (tiered) effective ~ $442/1M after blended tiers

B) Multi-year (24 months) + Growth rebate
- 24mo commitment: 35–42% off list depending on growth guarantees and up-front payment terms
- Additional annual growth rebate: 5–10% if YOY token consumption rises above agreed thresholds
- Example effective: 42% off $650 => $377/1M (plus growth rebates could move effective price closer to $340/1M at scale)

Other optional add-ons:
- Reserved (Dedicated) capacity: incremental surcharge; provides tail-latency SLOs and predictable throughput. We can price reserved pools separately if they need <50ms p95.
- Enterprise billing & extended payment terms: depends on procurement; we can invoice monthly or quarterly.

Quick unit-econ table (blended) — rough figures for discussion:
- Pilot / 15M/mo: list cost ~$9,750/mo -> after Starter credit and small commit, effective ~$6,500–7,500/mo
- Mid-ramp / 35M/mo: list ~$22,750/mo -> after 25–32% commit discount effective ~$15,500–17,000/mo
- Steady-state / 75M/mo: list ~$48,750/mo -> after 32–42% discount effective ~$28,000–33,000/mo (multi-year could push nearer $25k/mo)

Action items for Grace:
- Confirm if we should show both a Dedicated-reserved option and a Hosted-API committed option in the draft quote (I recommend both).
- Once Sam confirms the preferred billing cadence and whether they qualify for the Starter credit, I’ll pull together the formal quote PDF and a short legal summary for procurement.

 tagging: I’ll plan to include a non-binding quote link and two unit-price scenarios (12mo/24mo) for them to review on Friday call.

Rishi
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com

Sam — thanks for the usage spreadsheet, that’s exactly what we needed. We’ll send a short, non-binding quote that shows two purchase paths:

1) Starter + 12mo committed usage (best near-term runway) — includes $5k starter credit, tiered discounting, and example monthly totals at 25M / 50M / 75M volumes.
2) 24mo multi-year with growth rebate — deeper unit discounts and optional reserved capacity pricing (if Atlas needs stricter latency).

I’ve attached a draft quote (Atlas-Quote-Draft-ATL-2026-1183.pdf) — it’s non-binding and intended to show the math and options. Ben will include the invoice/billing options and a short note on PO vs card billing.

Proposed next step: 30m call Friday Aug 20 at 10:00 AM PT to walk the numbers and surface any legal/procurement asks. If that works I’ll send a calendar invite. If you’d rather the quote go to procurement first, we can route it directly to procurement@atlas-analytics.com.

Thanks — we’ll aim to get the draft quote and a HubSpot deal record update to you by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Grace
